messages:
maya: I pushed a tiny sampleapp showing a 'hot-resume' pattern for Generator streams. Goal: reattach after auth refresh without replaying already-consumed chunks. Can someone sanity-check the approach?
samir: share link pls
maya: repo: https://git.redwood/internal/sampleapps/gen-hot-resume. core idea: keep a SessionID and an offset cursor; if stream detaches, call Resume with a fresh ctx to reattach and pass the offset as an idempotency hint. Snippet: 
```go
ctx := context.Background()
s := client.Generators.NewSession(ctx, opts)
for msg := range s.Stream() {
  process(msg)
  s.MarkOffset(msg.Offset)
}
if s.Detached() {
  newCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
  defer cancel()
  resumed, err := client.Generators.Resume(newCtx, s.SessionID, s.Offset())
  // resumed.Stream() picks up after Offset
}
```
beth: this is valuable, but warning: we saw CI flakes where callers reused the original short-lived ctx for Resume and got immediate ErrDeadlineExceeded. We should either document "use fresh ctx for Resume" or change API to hide that.
kevin: UX decision: should Resume(ctx) treat ctx as only for handshake and internally use a fresh short-lived ctx if the provided ctx is already near-deadline? That might be surprising. Alternative: provide Attach() helper that creates an internal ctx for the handshake and returns either a resumed stream or an error indicating ctx was expired.
samir: impl detail: server currently returns a 409 when it detects duplicate replay attempt. SDK could translate that into ErrDuplicateChunk and suppress duplicate delivery if idempotency token matches.
maya: another mismatch: when runtime detaches due to auth refresh we turned it into io.EOF on the client stream. That makes it impossible for apps to distinguish normal completion vs auth-driven detach. Suggest adding ErrStreamDetached sentinel error and a Stream.DetachReason() accessor.
beth: agree on ErrStreamDetached. We'll add it behind a Beta flag for one release for compatibility. Also will add a small helper in the SDK: Session.Attach(ctx) that ensures the handshake uses a fresh bounded ctx and returns a resume func.
kevin: also add SDK metric: gen.resume.handshake_time and gen.resume.outcome {attached, retry, failed-expired-ctx} so we can monitor how often folks hit expired ctx behavior.
maya: sampleapp will include three recipes: (1) naive reuse ctx -> fail, (2) explicit new ctx -> succeed, (3) use Attach helper -> ergonomic success.
ci-bot: tests: generator-hot-resume unit tests started
samir: filed incident follow-up: token-service restarted caused short auth window; some sessions got mid-stream detaches. We should make Resume idempotent server-side as well to avoid duplicate emissions during retries.
beth: I'll open a PR: sampleapp + README note "safe resume patterns" + unit tests asserting ErrStreamDetached vs io.EOF and Resume behavior.
maya: thanks all. I'll link the PR here when ready. :thumbsup:
